## Overview

This document describes the data munging process used to create [PMTiles](https://docs.protomaps.com/pmtiles/) files for data sourced from the [`geobr`](https://ipeagit.github.io/geobr/) R package [@pereirab].

## Methods

### Source of Data

The data used in this pipeline come from the following sources:

- Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics ([IBGE](https://www.ibge.gov.br/)):
  - Brazil boundary data via the [`geobr`](https://ipeagit.github.io/geobr/) R package [@pereirab].
- [Uber Technologies](https://www.uber.com/):
  - Hexagonal grid data structured using the hexagonal hierarchical geospatial indexing system ([H3](https://h3geo.org/)) [@uber], processed with the [`h3jsr`](https://obrl-soil.github.io/h3jsr/) [@obrien2023] R packages.

### Data Munging

The data munging follow the data science workflow outlined by @wickham2023e, as illustrated in [@fig-wickham-at-al-2023-figure-1]. All processes were made using the [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) publishing system [@allaire], the [R](https://www.r-project.org/) programming language [@rcoreteam], and several R packages.

For data manipulation and workflow, priority was given to packages from the [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/), [rOpenSci](https://ropensci.org/) and [r-spatial](https://r-spatial.org/) ecosystems, as well as other packages adhering to the tidy tools manifesto [@wickham2023c].

::: {#fig-wickham-at-al-2023-figure-1}
![](images/wickham-at-al-2023-figure-1.png){width=75%}

[Source: Reproduced from @wickham2023e.]{.legend}

Data science workflow created by Wickham, Çetinkaya-Runde, and Grolemund.
:::

### Code Style

The Tidyverse [tidy tools manifesto](https://tidyverse.tidyverse.org/articles/manifesto.html) [@wickham2023c], [code style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/) [@wickhama] and [design principles](https://design.tidyverse.org/) [@wickhamc] were followed to ensure consistency and enhance readability.

### Reproducibility

The pipeline is fully reproducible and can be run again at any time. To ensure consistent results, the [`renv`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) package [@ushey2025] is used to manage and restore the R environment. See the [README](https://github.com/cem-usp/pmtilesbr/blob/main/README.md) file in the code repository to learn how to run it.

## Set Environment

### Load Packages

```{r}
#| label: Set the Environment
#| output: false

library(cli)
library(checkmate)
library(dplyr)
library(fs)
library(geobr)
library(glue)
library(h3jsr)
library(here)
library(lobstr)
library(mapgl)
library(orbis) # github.com/danielvartan/orbis
library(pmtiles) # github.com/walkerke/pmtiles
library(purrr)
library(quarto)
library(readr)
library(sf)
library(tidyr)
library(yyjsonr)
```

### Set Data Directories

```{r}
raw_data_dir <- here("data-raw", "geobr")
data_dir <- here("pmtiles")
```

```{r}
for (i in c(raw_data_dir, data_dir)) {
  if (!dir_exists(i)) {
    dir_create(i, recurse = TRUE)
  }
}
```

### Check Parameters

::: {.callout-note}
The pipeline main parameters are defined in the [YAML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YAML) header of its [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) document.

The `fun` variable specifies which function from the [`geobr`](https://ipeagit.github.io/geobr/) R package to use as the source of data.

The `code` variable specifies the IBGE code of the Brazilian territorial unit to retrieve. Use `"all"` to retrieve all units. For the full list of IBGE codes and their corresponding territorial units, see <https://sidra.ibge.gov.br/territorio>.

The `year` variable specifies the year of the data.

The `simplified` variable specifies whether to use simplified geometries for the spatial data. Simplified geometries are less detailed and have fewer vertices, which can improve performance when visualizing or processing the data, especially for large datasets.

The `min_zoom` and `max_zoom` variables specify the minimum and maximum zoom levels for the PMTiles files. The zoom levels determine the level of detail and granularity of the data when visualized on a map. See the [tippecanoe documentation](https://github.com/mapbox/tippecanoe#zoom-levels) for more details on how these parameters affect the PMTiles creation process.

The `h3jsr` variable specifies whether to process the spatial data with the [`h3jsr`](https://obrl-soil.github.io/h3jsr/) R package, which converts spatial geometries into [H3](https://h3geo.org/) hexagonal grid cells. If `TRUE`, the `res` variable will define the resolution of the H3 grid.

The `res` variable specifies the resolution of the [H3 hexagonal grid](https://h3geo.org/). This only applies when using the [`h3jsr`](https://obrl-soil.github.io/h3jsr/) R package. See [H3 documentation](https://h3geo.org/docs/core-library/restable/) for more details on the available resolutions and their corresponding cell sizes.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

if (!exists("params")) {
  params <-
    here("qmd", "geobr.qmd") |>
    quarto_inspect() |>
    pluck("formats", "html", "metadata", "params")

  params |> list2env(envir = .GlobalEnv)
}
```

```{r}
params |> lobstr::tree()
```

```{r}
fun_choices <- c(
  "read_municipality",
  "read_state",
  "read_region",
  "read_country"
)
```

```{r}
assert_choice(params$fun, getNamespaceExports("geobr"))
assert_choice(params$fun, fun_choices)
assert_int(params$year, lower = 1500, upper = 2050)
assert_flag(params$simplified)
assert_int(params$min_zoom, lower = 0, upper = 22)
assert_int(params$max_zoom, lower = 0, upper = 22)
assert_flag(params$h3jsr)
assert_int(params$res, lower = 0, upper = 15)
```

```{r}
if (params$code != "all") {
  if (params$fun == "read_municipality") {
    assert_int(params$code, lower = 1100015, upper = 5300108)
  } else if (params$fun == "read_state") {
    assert_int(params$code, lower = 11, upper = 53)
  }
}
```

## Download and Import Municipalities Shapes

```{r}
#| label: Download and Import Municipalities Shapes
#| eval: !expr 'params$fun == "read_municipality"'

read_municipality_file <-
  raw_data_dir |>
  file.path(
    paste0(
      paste(
        "read_municipality",
        "code",
        params$code,
        "year",
        params$year,
        "simplified",
        params$simplified,
        sep = "-"
      ),
      ".rds"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr 'params$fun == "read_municipality"'

read_municipality_file
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr 'params$fun == "read_municipality"'

if (!file_exists(read_municipality_file)) {
  shape <- read_municipality(
    code_muni = params$code,
    year = params$year,
    simplified = params$simplified,
    showProgress = FALSE
  )

  shape |> write_rds(read_municipality_file)
}
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr 'params$fun == "read_municipality"'

shape <- read_municipality_file |> read_rds()
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr 'params$fun == "read_municipality"'

shape |> glimpse()
```

## Create PMTiles

### Transform Shapes

#### Change Coordinate Reference System (CRS)

```{r}
#| label: Create PMTiles

shape <-
  shape |>
  st_transform(crs = 4326)
```

```{r}
shape |> glimpse()
```

#### Recode Region Names

```{r}
if ("name_region" %in% colnames(shape)) {
  shape <-
    shape |>
    mutate(
      name_region_en = name_region |>
        recode_values(
          "Norte" ~ "North",
          "Nordeste" ~ "Northeast",
          "Sudeste" ~ "Southeast",
          "Sul" ~ "South",
          "Centro Oeste" ~ "Central-West"
        )
    ) |>
    relocate(name_region_en, .after = name_region)
}
```

```{r}
shape |> glimpse()
```

### Create PMTiles

#### Set Pattern

```{r}
if (isTRUE(params$h3jsr)) {
  pattern <- file.path(
    "geobr",
    params$fun,
    "h3jsr",
    paste0("res-", params$res)
  )
} else {
  pattern <- file.path(
    "geobr",
    params$fun
  )
}
```

```{r}
pattern
```

```{r}
pattern <-
  pattern |>
  file.path(
    paste0(
      ifelse(
        !params$fun %in% c("read_country", "read_region"),
        paste0("code", "-", params$code, "-"),
        ""
      ),
      # fmt: skip
      paste(
      "year", params$year,
      "simplified", params$simplified,
      "min_zoom", params$min_zoom,
      "max_zoom", params$max_zoom,
      sep = "-"
    ),
      ".pmtiles"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
pattern
```

```{r}
#| include: false
#| message: NA

cli_alert_info(
  "PMTiles file pattern:\n\n{.code {pattern}}."
)
```

```{r}
for (i in c(data_dir, tempdir())) {
  i |>
    file.path(pattern) |>
    dirname() |>
    dir_create(recurse = TRUE)
}
```

#### Process Shapes with `h3jsr`

```{r}
if (isTRUE(params$h3jsr)) {
  shape <-
    shape |>
    polygon_to_cells(res = params$res, simple = FALSE) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    unnest(h3_addresses) |>
    relocate(h3_addresses) |>
    cell_to_polygon(simple = FALSE) |>
    relocate(h3_address)
}
```

```{r}
shape |> glimpse()
```

#### Create PMTiles

```{r}
code <- ifelse(
  is.character(params$code),
  double_quote(params$code),
  params$code
)
```

```{r}
shape |>
  pm_create(
    output = tempdir() |> file.path(pattern),
    layer_name = params$fun,
    min_zoom = params$min_zoom,
    max_zoom = params$max_zoom,
    description = glue(
      "Tiles sourced from the {backtick(params$fun)} function of the ",
      "{backtick('geobr')} R package ",
      "(",
      ifelse(
        params$fun %in% c("read_country", "read_region"),
        "",
        paste0("code", " = ", params$code, ", ")
      ),
      "year = {params$year}, ",
      "simplified = {params$simplified}",
      ")",
      ifelse(
        isTRUE(params$h3jsr),
        paste0(
          " and processed with the {backtick('h3jsr')} R package ",
          "(res = {params$res}). "
        ),
        ". "
      ),
      "Created with the {backtick('pmtiles')} R package on {Sys.Date()}."
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: Test PMTiles

tempdir() |>
  file.path(pattern) |>
  pm_show(tilejson = TRUE)
```

```{r}
tempdir() |>
  file.path(pattern) |>

  )
```
